To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a physiologic model of perchlorate and iodide kinetics in the male rat that can accurately predict perchlorate and radioiodide kinetics after iv dosing, as well as thyroid inhibition of 125I- after ClO4- exposure, and that it provides a basis for future inclusion of the thyroid feedback system in the model.
we have developed a physiologic model of perchlorate that predicts the kinetics of perchlorate and iodide in the rat and their interaction at the thyroid.

a PBPK model for perchlorate was developed that successfully predicted perchlorate's kinetics and its effect on radioiodide kinetics in rats, and that the model can be used for extrapolation of perchlorate dose metrics and correlation of effects in perchlorates toxicity studies to other rat life stages, such that the model can serve as a basis for future incorporation the hypothalamic-piutary-thyroid axis into the model.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and validation of a PBPK model for perchlorate in the male rat that can predict perchlorate's effects on normal thyroid function, including inhibition of thyroidal 125I- and 131I- uptake.
the development of physiologically based pharmacokinetic ( PBPK) models to describe the kinetics of perchlorate and its interaction with iodide.
the use of PBPK modeling to predict the effects of perchlorate exposure on thyroid I- kinetics in the rat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this model is a valuable tool for predicting perchlorate distribution in the adult male rat, its interaction with iodide at the NIS and the thyroid feedback system, and the potential for adverse health effects from chronic exposure.
the PBPK model for perchlorate in the male rat provides a useful framework for extrapolating perchlorate toxicity from rat to man.
this model is a useful tool for predicting the kinetics of ClO4-, its interaction with iodide and the effects of perchlorate on thyroid uptake of iodide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a PBPK model for the adult rat has been developed that successfully predicts the kinetics of ClO4-, I-, and their interaction.

we have successfully incorporated the complex interaction between ClO4- and I- at the NIS in a PBPK model and that the model predicts observed kinetics and effects of ClO4-, I-, and ClO4- + I- in the male rat.
the PBPK model provides a sound basis to predict perchlorate's distribution and its effect of thyroid radioiodide uptake in the rat.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PBPK modeling can be a powerful tool in the risk assessment of perchlorate.

a physiologically-relevant PBPK model of ClO4-, which accounts for its competitive inhibition of I- at the NIS and upregulation of I- uptake in the thyroid, can be developed to predict perchlorate kinetics and its effect on I- kinetics.
the model structure and parameters developed here are sufficient to describe ClO4- and I- kinetics in rats and to predict the effect of perchlorate on thyroid I- uptake.
